reviewed_scope: EXT-D-0199 source cause and shared notice layout repair
SidepanelFrame, NoticeHost, App integration, notice layout guard, relevant feature-test instructions

evidence: The hosted receipt for run 38157769699 shows one active enabled Re-audit target, zero target-owned hit points, and nine database-refusal-notice hit points at history_refused, history_recovered, and before_click. The pointer driver's center sample independently names the recognized database_refused notice. This supports the stated occlusion cause; the failed run itself earns no T02 acceptance credit.

SidepanelFrame places the unchanged AuthGate content in a min-h-0 flexible region and mounts the shared NoticeHost as its trailing sibling. NoticeHost remains outside AuthGate, so guest, member, admin, and auth/error surfaces continue using the same host and store.

Notice retirement, tone-specific alert/status roles and icons, admin-only detail, cross-context relay, and the native Dismiss button are unchanged. The host no longer uses fixed/absolute positioning or pointer-event pass-through classes; its tray has a 40% height bound and vertical scrolling, leaving room for the panel content. Emptying the store removes the tray and returns that space.
cannot_verify: No post-fix native run was available. Actual pointer clearance, tray and panel scroll interaction, long notices, 360px and normal widths, panel/extension reload, and native retry/dismiss behavior remain open per EXT-D-0199.
Member/admin and Store-installed behavior remain unverified. Source placement is shared, but this review does not promote those runtime boundaries.
verdict_a_product_reasoning.acceptance_state: Native post-fix acceptance remains required; do not close EXT-D-0199 or promote EXT-F-1008/T02 from this source review.

findings: The focused guard asserts the panel-flow contract, flexible content sibling, bounded scroll tray, absence of fixed/absolute classes, retained info status, individual Dismiss behavior, and content-space recovery after the final dismissal. It explicitly says it does not prove native geometry or pointer clearance.

Mutation proof: plant.py temporarily restored the former fixed positioning classes on the production tray; notice-layout.test.tsx failed at the intended fixed-class assertion (expected true to be false). plant.py restored NoticeHost byte-identically (SHA fae9307ecf43). This proves the named regression is caught, not the broader native acceptance behavior.
The new test groups layout and dismissal in one case; splitting these independent outcomes would make failures easier to route. This is a guard-quality improvement, not a product-source blocker.
verdict_b_guard_and_source_quality.reuse_and_scope: The repair uses one shared NoticeHost and a small side-panel frame. It does not add a second notice system, alter notice lifecycle semantics, or suppress any notice tone.
